newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar futures gains pared by close.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar futures gains pared by close.

text.p: White sugar futures saw earlier gains cut by up to $2 a tonne by the close reflecting a lack of a significant upward move in New York.
Light profittaking and liquidation saw the near December position last trade at $325.00 a tonne, after an earlier high of $327.00, to show a gain of $0.90 a tonne from Wednesday.
Other traded months were between $0.30 up and $0.90 a tonne down and turnover totalled 1,565 lots.
In physicals confusion was evident in the market over whether Sri Lanka had bought 12,500 tonnes of lesser-quality white sugar at its recent tender or decided to reinvite bids for later this week.
London traders said the country's state buying arm, the Co-operative Wholesale Establishment (CWE), bought the sugar at $343.00 a tonne c & f from a European trading house.
But traders in Colombo said the CWE had asked suppliers to resubmit bids before Friday.

Syria bought 26,000 tonnes of sugar for November shipment dates, taking 13,000 tonnes of raw sugar from a European trade house at $312.94 per tonne and 13,000 tonnes of whites at around $364 a tonne from a London-based house, market sources said.
Paris white sugar ended with December at $325.80, a gain of $1.80 a tonne.
